summary: Which jewelry and hair ribbons may a woman wear outside on Shabbos? The Rabbis forbade some, in case she takes them off to show a friend and carries them in the street.
stIntro: The mishna lists items that a woman may or may not carry into, or wear in the public domain on Shabbat. This depends the particular object is considered an ornament, which she may wear, or merely a burden for the woman, which she may not. Even if it is considered an ornament, there is still concern that she might remove it and carry it in her hand in the public domain, which is prohibited by Torah law.

chunks.he: בַּמֶּה אִשָּׁה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
chunks.en: With what may a woman go out, and with what may she not go out?
chunks.st: With what items may a woman go out into the public domain on Shabbat and with what items may she not go out?

chunks.he: לֹא תֵצֵא אִשָּׁה לֹא בְחוּטֵי צֶמֶר
chunks.en: A woman may not go out with wool strings,
chunks.st: A woman may neither go out with strings of wool,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְחוּטֵי פִשְׁתָּן וְלֹא בִרְצוּעוֹת שֶׁבְּרֹאשָׁהּ.
chunks.en: or linen strings, or ribbons in her hair.
chunks.st: nor with strings of flax, nor with strips of any other materials that a woman braids in the hair of her head.

chunks.en: And she may not dip in a mikvah with them until she loosens them.
chunks.st: And a woman may not immerse in a ritual bath with them in her hair until she loosens them.
chunks.stMore: When the strings or strips are tight, the water cannot reach her hair unobstructed, invalidating her immersion.

chunks.en: And not with a totefes or with sarbitin,
chunks.st: And, likewise, a woman may neither go out with the ornament called totefet, nor with sarvitin

words.note: A band worn across the forehead.

chunks.en: when they are not sewn on,
chunks.st: that are not sewn into her head covering,

chunks.en: and not with a kavul into the street.
chunks.st: nor with a kavul into the public domain.

chunks.en: And not with a "golden city,"
chunks.explain: A gold crown shaped like Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: And, likewise, a woman may neither go out with a city of gold ornament,

chunks.en: and not with a necklace,
chunks.st: nor with a katla ornament,

chunks.en: and not with nose rings,
chunks.st: nor with nose rings,

chunks.en: and not with a ring that has no seal on it,
chunks.st: nor with a ring that has no seal on it,

chunks.en: and not with a needle that has no hole.
chunks.st: nor with a needle that is not perforated, which are merely for decorative purposes.

chunks.en: But if she did go out,
chunks.st: And if she unwittingly went out wearing any of these,

chunks.en: she does not have to bring a korban chatas.
chunks.explain: These things are not forbidden by the Torah.
chunks.st: she is not liable to bring a sin-offering.
chunks.stMore: According to Torah law, a woman is permitted to go out into the public domain wearing ornaments. However, the Sages decreed that a woman may not go out wearing certain ornaments, lest she remove them to show them to another and inadvertently carry them four cubits in the public domain.

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

summary: A man may not go out on Shabbos with some kinds of shoes, tefillin, or armor. If he did, he does not need to bring a korban chatas.

chunks.en: A man may not go out with a sandal full of nails,
chunks.st: A man may not go out on Shabbat with a spiked sandal, as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְיָחִיד בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בְּרַגְלוֹ מַכָּה,
chunks.en: and not with one sandal when his foot is not hurt,
chunks.st: And he may not go out with a single sandal when there is no wound on his foot.

chunks.en: and not with tefillin,
chunks.st: And he may neither go out with phylacteries,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְקָמֵעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמֻּמְחֶה,
chunks.en: and not with a kamea when it is not from an expert,
chunks.st: nor with an amulet when it is not from an expert,
chunks.stMore: but rather it was written by someone who has not established a reputation as an expert in writing amulets that are effective for those who carry them.

words.note: A written charm worn to help heal.

chunks.en: and not with armor,
chunks.st: And he may neither go out with shiryon,

chunks.en: and not with a helmet,
chunks.st: nor with a kasda,

chunks.en: and not with leg guards.
chunks.st: nor with maggafayim. These terms will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: But if he did go out,
chunks.st: And if he went out into the public domain with any of these,

chunks.en: he does not have to bring a korban chatas.
chunks.st: he is not liable to bring a sin-offering.

summary: A woman may not go out with things that are tools or containers and not jewelry, like a needle with a hole or a seal ring. Rabbi Meir says she must bring a korban chatas, but the Sages say some of these are like jewelry.

chunks.en: A woman may not go out with a needle that has a hole,
chunks.st: A woman may neither go out to the public domain with a perforated needle, i.e., a standard needle with an eye,

chunks.en: and not with a ring that has a seal on it,
chunks.st: nor with a ring that has a seal on it,

chunks.en: and not with a kulyar,
chunks.st: nor with a kulyar,

chunks.en: and not with a perfume box,
chunks.st: nor with a kovelet,
chunks.stMore: the identity of which will be discussed in the Gemara,

chunks.en: and not with a little bottle of balsam oil.
chunks.st: nor with a flask of balsam oil.

chunks.en: And if she did go out,
chunks.st: And if she did go out into the public domain,

chunks.en: she must bring a korban chatas.
chunks.st: she is liable to bring a sin-offering; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.stMore: who holds that in doing so she violated the Torah prohibition of carrying a burden in the public domain on Shabbat.

chunks.he: וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין בְּכוֹבֶלֶת וּבִצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל פַּלְיָטוֹן:
chunks.en: But the Sages say she is patur for the perfume box and the bottle of balsam oil.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis exempt one who goes out on Shabbat with a kovelet and with a flask of balsam oil.
chunks.stMore: In their opinion, these are ornaments, and therefore they do not fundamentally violate the Torah prohibition of carrying in the public domain on Shabbat.

summary: A man may not go out on Shabbos with weapons. Rabbi Eliezer says they are like jewelry for him, but the Sages say they are a disgrace, because one day there will be no more war.
stIntro: Just as it is prohibited for a woman to carry out certain items unique to a woman into the public domain, the Sages said that

chunks.en: A man may not go out with a sword,
chunks.st: a man may neither go out on Shabbat with a sword,

chunks.en: or with a bow,
chunks.st: nor with a bow,

chunks.en: or with a shield,
chunks.st: nor with a shield [teris],

chunks.en: or with a club,
chunks.st: nor with an alla,

chunks.en: or with a spear.
chunks.st: nor with a spear.

chunks.en: And if he did go out,
chunks.st: And if he unwittingly went out
chunks.stMore: with one of these weapons to the public domain

chunks.en: he must bring a korban chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: they are jewelry for him.
chunks.st: These weapons are ornaments for him;
chunks.stMore: just as a man is permitted to go out into the public domain with other ornaments, he is permitted to go out with weapons.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they are only a disgrace,
chunks.st: They are nothing other than reprehensible and in the future they will be eliminated,

chunks.en: as it says: "And they will beat
chunks.st: as it is written: “And they shall beat their

chunks.en: their swords into plows, and their spears into pruning tools.
chunks.st: swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks;

chunks.en: A nation will not lift up
chunks.st: nation will not raise sword

chunks.en: a sword against a nation, and they will not learn war anymore."
chunks.st: against nation, neither will they learn war anymore”
chunks.stMore: (Isaiah 2:4). With regard to women’s ornaments, they added that

chunks.en: A garter is tahor,
chunks.st: a garter placed on her leg to hold up stockings is pure
chunks.stMore: and cannot become ritually impure as a utensil,

words.note: A band worn on the leg.

chunks.en: and she may go out with it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: and she may even go out with it on Shabbat. However,

chunks.en: Ankle chains can become tamei,
chunks.st: ankle chains, which were also women’s ornaments, can become ritually impure,

chunks.en: and she may not go out with them on Shabbos.
chunks.st: and she may not go out with them on Shabbat.

summary: A woman may go out with a hair piece, a sewn-on ornament, a cotton in her ear, or salt in her mouth for her health. Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi and the Sages argue about a false tooth.
stIntro: The mishna continues to discuss those items with which it is permitted to go out and those items with which it is prohibited to go out on Shabbat.

chunks.en: A woman may go out with strands of hair,
chunks.st: A woman may go out with strands of hair that she put on her head,

chunks.en: whether from her own hair, or from
chunks.st: whether they are from her own hair that she made into a wig, or whether they are

chunks.en: her friend's, or from an animal's,
chunks.st: from the hair of another, or whether they are from the hair of an animal.

chunks.en: and with a totefes or with sarbitin when they are sewn on.
chunks.st: And a woman may go out with an ornament called totefet, and with sarvitin when they are sewn and will not fall.

chunks.en: With a kavul or with a wig into the courtyard.
chunks.st: She may go out on Shabbat with a woolen cap or with a wig to the courtyard, although not to the public domain.

chunks.en: With cotton in her ear, and with cotton in her sandal,
chunks.st: And likewise she may go out with a cloth that is in her ear, and with a cloth in her sandal,

chunks.en: and with cotton she prepared for herself.
chunks.st: and with a cloth that she placed due to her menstrual status.

chunks.en: With pepper, a grain of salt, and anything
chunks.st: She may go out on Shabbat with pepper, or with a grain of salt,

chunks.en: that she puts into her mouth,
chunks.explain: These are for her health or to keep her breath fresh.
chunks.st: or anything placed in her mouth for healing or for preventing bad odor,

chunks.en: as long as she does not put it in for the first time on Shabbos.
chunks.st: as long as she does not put these objects in her mouth for the first time on Shabbat.

chunks.en: And if it fell out,
chunks.st: And if it fell out

chunks.en: she may not put it back.
chunks.st: she may not replace it.

chunks.en: A false tooth or a gold tooth,
chunks.st: A false tooth as well as (Ramban) a gold tooth,

chunks.en: Rebbi allows it,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi permits going out with it,

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis prohibit doing so.

summary: A woman may go out with a coin tied on a sore, and girls may go out with strings in their ears. Clothes that people normally wear in their country are fine for anyone.

chunks.en: She may go out with a coin on a sore.
chunks.st: may go out with a sela coin that she ties on a wound on her foot.

chunks.en: Little girls may go out with strings
chunks.st: The young girls may go out with strings,

chunks.en: and even with little sticks in their ears.
chunks.explain: These keep the holes in their ears open.
chunks.st: and even with wood chips that are in the holes in their ears
chunks.stMore: so that the holes will not seal. Young girls would have their ears pierced, but earrings were not placed in their ears until they were older.

chunks.en: Arabian women may go out veiled,
chunks.st: Jewish women in Arab countries may go out veiled, with a scarf covering their face,

chunks.en: and women of Madai with cloaks pinned.
chunks.st: and Jewish women in Media may go out with cloaks fastened with stones.

chunks.en: And so may any person,
chunks.st: And, any person
chunks.stMore: in any place is permitted to go out on Shabbat clothed in that way;

chunks.en: but the Sages spoke about what usually happens.
chunks.st: however, the Sages spoke in the present, addressing prevalent situations.

summary: A woman may fasten her cloak around a stone, a nut, or a coin, like a button. But she should not first do it on Shabbos.

chunks.en: She may fasten her cloak on a stone, on
chunks.st: may fasten her cloak on a stone by inserting a small stone and wrapping her cloak around it, as she would with a button. And likewise, she may do so

chunks.en: a nut, or on a coin,
chunks.st: on a nut or on a coin,

chunks.en: as long as she does not first fasten it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: as long as she does not fasten her cloak with them on Shabbat ab initio.

summary: A man without a leg may go out on Shabbos with his wooden leg, says Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yosei forbids it. The mishnah also teaches which supports for people who cannot walk can become tamei.

chunks.en: A person missing a leg may go out with his wooden leg.
chunks.st: One with an amputated leg may go out on Shabbat with his wooden leg, as it has the legal status of a shoe;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yosei forbids it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei prohibits
chunks.stMore: going out into the public domain with the wooden leg, since he does not consider it to have the legal status of a shoe.

chunks.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל כְּתוּתִים,
chunks.en: And if it has a place to hold soft pads,
chunks.st: And if the wooden leg has a receptacle for pads,
chunks.stMore: a concave space at the top of the leg into which pads are placed to cushion the amputated leg, it assumes the status of a wooden vessel and can become

chunks.en: it can become tamei. His knee supports
chunks.st: ritually impure. And his supports,
chunks.stMore: which are shoes that one who had both of his feet amputated places on his knees in order to walk on his knees, if a zav wears them, they are

chunks.en: can become tamei like something walked on,
chunks.st: subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading.
chunks.stMore: A zav is a primary source of ritual impurity. If he touches a vessel it assumes first-degree ritual impurity status. However, vessels on which he treads, sits, lies, or leans become primary sources of ritual impurity, provided they are designated for that purpose. These supports are vessels designated for treading.

words.note: Tumah of things that a zav steps on.

chunks.en: and he may go out with them on Shabbos,
chunks.st: And one may go out with them into the public domain on Shabbat since they have the legal status of shoes.

chunks.en: and go into the Azarah with them.
chunks.st: And one may enter the Temple courtyard with them.
chunks.stMore: Although, generally, wearing shoes in the Temple courtyard is prohibited, in this regard, the supports do not have the legal status of shoes. However, if one who is crippled to the extent that he cannot walk at all sits on a chair that is attached to him, places supports on his hands, and propels himself along with his hands,

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: His chair and his hand supports
chunks.st: his chair and supports are

chunks.en: can become tamei like something walked on,
chunks.st: subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading.

chunks.en: and he may not go out with them on Shabbos,
chunks.st: And one may not go out with them on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and not go into the Azarah with them.
chunks.st: and one may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.

chunks.en: Ankatmin are tahor,
chunks.st: Loketamin, which will be explained in the Gemara, are ritually pure
chunks.stMore: in the sense that they cannot become ritually impure because they are not vessels,

words.note: Some kind of wooden supports; the Gemara explains.

chunks.en: but we may not go out with them.
chunks.st: and one may not go out with them on Shabbat.

summary: Boys may go out on Shabbos with knots that were used as a cure, and princes with bells. Anyone may do this; the Sages just spoke about what was usual.

chunks.en: Boys may go out with knots,
chunks.st: boys may go out on Shabbat with knots as a folk remedy

chunks.en: and princes with bells.
chunks.st: and princes with bells.

chunks.en: And so may any person,
chunks.st: And any person
chunks.stMore: is permitted to go out on Shabbat with those objects;

chunks.en: but the Sages spoke about what usually happens.
chunks.st: however, the Sages spoke in the present, addressing situations that were prevalent.

summary: Rabbi Meir allows going out on Shabbos with certain things people used as cures. The Sages say these are superstitions of the non-Jews, forbidden even during the week.

chunks.en: We may go out with a locust egg,
chunks.st: One may go out on Shabbat with a locust egg,

chunks.en: and with a fox's tooth,
chunks.st: and with a fox tooth,

chunks.en: and with a nail from a gallows,
chunks.st: and with a nail from the crucified,

chunks.en: to help healing.
chunks.st: for the purpose of healing;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: The Rabbis prohibit using these remedies

chunks.en: it is forbidden even during the week,
chunks.st: even during the week,

chunks.en: because it is a way of the Emori.
chunks.st: due to the prohibition of following the ways of the Amorite.
chunks.stMore: These are superstitious beliefs and the customs of gentiles from which one must distance oneself.

words.note: A nation that did things of avodah zarah and superstition.
